issues.legal_issue: A notice calling arbitrators to act does not restart the award period if it is given after the period running from their entry on the reference has expired, and an award made after the applicable period requires a court extension to be effective.
material_facts: The parties referred their dispute to arbitrators, who entered on the reference and began taking evidence within ten days.
The arbitrators later stopped proceeding with the inquiry.
More than four months after the arbitrators entered on the reference, a party gave them notice to proceed and make an award.
The arbitrators made the award within four months after that notice, but after the period running from their entry on the reference had expired.
No court extension of the time to make the award was obtained.
issues.conclusion: The later notice did not restart the time for making the award. Because the award was made after the applicable period and the court had not extended that period, it could not be enforced; the appeal was dismissed.
issues.legal_principle: Section 3 of the Arbitration Act, 1940 incorporates the First Schedule into an arbitration agreement unless a different intention is expressed. Rule 3 of the First Schedule is mandatory and sets alternative starting points for the award period. A notice to act may be given before or after the arbitrators enter on the reference, but a notice given after entry can alter the computation only if given before the original period expires; a party cannot revive an expired reference by giving a later notice. A notice to act is available when arbitrators have refused or neglected to discharge their duty. Under section 28, the court may extend the time, including after an award has factually been made. The Court relied on Baring Gould v. Sharpington Combined Pick and Shovel Syndicate and Sardar Mal Hardat Rai v. Sheo Bakhsh Rai Sri Narain.

rule.if: arbitration_award_enforcement_proceeding and arbitrators_entered_reference and notice_given_after_deadline and award_made_after_deadline and not court_extended_deadline

predicates.arbitration_award_enforcement_proceeding: The proceeding seeks enforcement of an award made by arbitrators.
predicates.arbitrators_entered_reference: The arbitrators accepted the reference and began acting on it.
predicates.notice_given_after_deadline: A party gave the arbitrators notice to act only after the original period for making the award had expired.
predicates.award_made_after_deadline: The arbitrators made the award after the original period for making it had expired.
predicates.court_extended_deadline: The court extended the time for making the award.

issues.definition: When an enforcement proceeding concerns an award made after the original deadline, and a party gave notice to act only after that deadline, the award is out of time and cannot be enforced unless the court extended the deadline.
